requirement: The controller's identity and how to contact it about personal data
evidence: Any personal information processed by Saudia in connection with this Privacy Policy is controlled by Saudia, which is considered the “data controller” of your personal information
reason: The policy names Saudia as controller and gives a postal address for Saudi Arabian Airlines Corporation plus a contact form.

requirement: Contact details of the data protection officer (DPO)
condition: The controller has appointed a DPO
evidence: The Data Protection Officer for Saudia can be contacted via the Contact Form
reason: A DPO contact route is given through a contact form and a postal address, but no direct DPO email or phone number.

requirement: The personal data that is collected
evidence: Types of personal information we collect depend on the nature of your interaction with us
reason: The policy lists specific data types, such as name, date of birth, passport details, payment card details and sensitive data.

requirement: The means used to collect personal data
evidence: We collect personal information about you whenever you use our services
reason: The policy describes collection via websites, apps, email, contact centres, cookies, and third parties.

requirement: The purpose of collecting and processing personal data
evidence: To fulfil your travel arrangements and deliver the services you have asked for, including ticketing, bookings, changes, cancellations, refunds, upgrades, and ancillary services
reason: The policy sets out detailed purposes in a dedicated section on what personal information is used for.

requirement: The legal basis for collecting personal data (e.g. consent, contract, legal obligation)
evidence: Because we need to use your information so that we can process your booking, fulfill your travel arrangements and otherwise perform the contract we have with you.
reason: The policy lists specific legal bases: contract, legitimate interests, legal obligation, vital interests and consent.

requirement: Which personal data is mandatory and which is optional
evidence: When you use our services, you will need to provide us with your personal details or the details of those individual(s) who will be travelling.
reason: It implies some data is required to use services but never clearly separates mandatory from optional data, apart from noting that some items are provided by choice.

requirement: The consequences of not providing personal data
evidence: However, if you withdraw your full consent, in some circumstances, it may mean we will not be able to provide all or parts of the services you have requested from us and you will not be able to cancel your booking or obtain a refund of any charges you have paid.
reason: It states consequences of withdrawing consent but not generally of refusing to provide data at collection.

requirement: The parties personal data is disclosed or shared with, and their capacity
evidence: Airlines and other service providers needed to deliver the services you have asked for where, for instance, part of your travel itinerary involves a flight operated by a different airline or includes car hire or a hotel booking.
reason: It lists recipient categories (group companies, authorities, airlines, payment firms, service providers) and their roles, including data controllers.

requirement: Whether personal data is transferred, disclosed or processed outside the Kingdom
evidence: Your personal information may be sent to and stored by us and third parties in countries outside the country in which you are located.
reason: It confirms transfers abroad but speaks generally of countries outside the user's location and the EEA, without specifically addressing transfers outside the Kingdom.

requirement: How long personal data is kept, or the criteria used to decide
evidence: If you stop interacting with us as a customer, we will remove or anonymise your information after 7 years.
reason: The policy gives a 7-year retention period and the criteria of keeping data as long as needed for the purpose.

requirement: How personal data is stored and destroyed
evidence: Safely disposing of or anonymizing personal data when it is no longer needed
reason: It mentions secure deletion or anonymisation and security protocols for storage, but gives no specific detail on how data is stored and destroyed.

requirement: The data subject's rights: to be informed, access, obtain a copy, correct, and request destruction
evidence: You may access the personal information we hold on you.
reason: The policy lists access, copy, correction and erasure rights, though the right to be informed is only implied through the notice itself.

requirement: How the data subject can exercise their rights
evidence: Alternatively, you can make a request to us via our Contact Form , ensuring you mark the request for Customer Permissions (Data Protection Office).
reason: It explains how to submit requests, the identity verification required and the details to include.

evidence: If the basis of our processing your data is consent to marketing, you can withdraw your consent to such processing at any time, including by amending your account online or alternately contact us via our Contact Form page.
reason: It states clearly how consent can be withdrawn, through account settings or the contact form.

requirement: The measures taken to protect personal data
condition: Large-scale or continuous processing, monitoring, new technologies, or automated decisions
evidence: We have implemented robust technical and organizational security measures, policies, and procedures to protect your personal information and ensure its privacy
reason: The policy states technical and organizational security measures and lists specific ones such as confidentiality obligations, secure disposal and storage protocols.

requirement: Whether decisions are made solely by automated processing
condition: Large-scale or continuous processing, monitoring, new technologies, or automated decisions
reason: The section on AI and automated processing never says whether decisions are made solely by automated processing, and it gives no such statement about decisions affecting individuals.
